headline: Kodiak and IKEA plan to run trucks with nobody on board between Houston and Dallas later this year.
score_reason: Concrete launch plan with a named customer, but company-sourced and pending a safety case.
importance_line: A driverless long-haul route with a real customer could change trucking work and freight costs, but the launch depends on Kodiak finishing its safety case and every figure comes from the company.
summary: Robotics & Automation News reports, citing Kodiak, that the autonomous-trucking company will start fully driverless freight runs for IKEA Supply in Texas later this year, on a 219-mile stretch mostly along Interstate 45. Kodiak says it has hauled more than 1,300 IKEA loads over four years and 750,000 autonomous miles with a safety observer aboard, and is still completing the safety case, the evidence that its system can run with no person in the truck.
notes: machine_action true because the trucks already run autonomously with a safety observer; the driverless leg itself is planned.
